the optimal control of discrete time systems with state and control constraints.
the development of a general theory of constrained optimal control.
the design and stability analysis of a class of feedback laws for constrained discrete-time systems using a combination of optimal control theory and Lyapunov techniques.

the moving horizon feedback system is a good approximation to the optimal infinite horizon feedback system for a general class of nonlinear discrete time constrained systems with a wide range of cost functions and constraints.
the moving horizon approximation of the optimal feedback law is asymptotically optimal.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a unified framework for the analysis and synthesis of constrained discrete time systems using the optimal infinite horizon feedback law and the moving horizon feedback laws with a guaranteed convergence of the moving horizon cost to the infinite horizon cost.

we have shown the existence and uniqueness of the optimal infinite horizon feedback law, the existence of the moving horizon feedback laws, their stability properties, and that the moving horizon feedback systems can approximate the optimal infinite horizon systems.
we have developed a general theory for the optimal control of a class of constrained discrete time nonlinear systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stability of the moving horizon feedback system can be guaranteed under weaker conditions on the cost and constraints than those required for the stability of the optimal infinite horizon feedback law.
, for a general class of nonlinear discrete time systems with state constraints, stability is achieved by using a moving horizon approximation to an optimal infinite horizon law.

, in the presence of constraints, the optimal infinite horizon feedback system can be approximated arbitrarily closely by a finite horizon system, and the approximation error can be made arbitrarily small by extending the horizon.
